title: The effect of stellar multiplicity on protoplanetary discs: a near-infrared survey of the Lupus star-forming region
question: Identify (sub)stellar companions down to ~20 au separation in the Lupus Molecular Cloud and investigate the effects of stellar multiplicity on circumstellar disc properties (masses, sizes, brightness profiles).

data.bands: Band 6 (1.3 mm / 1.33 mm) for Class II; Band 7 (860 um) for Class III
data.angular_resolution: 0.25 arcsec (~0.2 arcsec) for Class II; ~0.7 arcsec for Class III
data.sensitivity: 0.10 mJy beam^-1 (median 1.3 mm continuum rms for Class II); ~37 uJy at 860 um (Class III)

what.value: Class II disc dust masses (Table 1), disc sizes/semi-major axes (Table 3), companion mm fluxes and flux ratios (Table 4), and ALMA coordinates

evidence.quote: The dust mass for each disc is taken from the last column of Table 1 in (cite: Ansdell2018) for the Class II objects
The values of their masses are obtained from the millimetre fluxes listed in Table 4 of (cite: Ansdell2018)
The disc size for the Class II objects is used when available in (cite: Ansdell2018) (Table 3), otherwise we assume the disc is unresolved.

what.value: Class III disc dust masses (Table 1) and disc resolution/size information

evidence.quote: The dust mass for each disc is taken from the last column of Table 1 in (cite: Ansdell2018) for the Class II objects, and from Table 1 of (cite: 2020MNRAS.tmp.3151L) for the Class III objects.
Concerning the Class III objects, 3 discs were unresolved, and only one was marginally resolved (cite: 2020MNRAS.tmp.3151L).

what.value: Gaia DR2 distances for primary and secondary components

evidence.quote: Most of the systems have *Gaia* Data Release 2 (DR2) parallax measurements (cite: Bailer_Jones_2018), which we report in Table [\[t:bin\]](#t:bin)

what.value: Ophiuchus NIR-ODISEA multiplicity, disc mass, size, and radial profile dataset for combined statistical analysis

evidence.quote: In Figure [11](#f:histo_sp_com) we show the histograms that include also the Ophiuchus sample, which follows the same trend.
To strengthen the statistical analysis, we combined this Lupus survey with its twin in Ophiuchus (cite: Zurlo2020).

recipe.goal: Reduce VLT/NACO images and detect visual companion candidates
recipe.method: Background subtract, flat-field, re-centre and average pairs of frames; astrometrically calibrate using ALMA coordinates and pixel scale; identify >5sigma signals using Daophot via photutils followed by visual inspection; compute azimuthal rms contrast curves.
key_parameters: detection threshold > 5 sigma; pixel scale = 0.02719 arcsec/pixel; FOV ~ 32 arcsec
assumptions: ALMA coordinates correspond to the center of the star

recipe.goal: Assess physical boundness and background probability of detected companions
recipe.method: Compare Gaia DR2 distances of components where available; for unconfirmed candidates, model background stars as a homogeneous spatial Poisson point process within a circle of radius equal to the companion separation using TRILEGAL galaxy model number densities; estimate substellar mass using AMES-COND models.
assumptions: Homogeneous spatial Poisson point process for background stars; discordant Gaia distances imply unbound systems

recipe.goal: Compile disc dust masses and sizes and compare cumulative distributions across multiplicity categories
recipe.method: Take Class II/III disc dust masses and sizes (90% flux curve-of-growth radius) from Ansdell et al. (2018) and Lovell et al. (2020); compute companion dust masses from Ansdell et al. (2018) mm fluxes; construct Kaplan-Meier cumulative distribution functions accounting for non-detections using lifelines; perform two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests for Lupus and combined Lupus+Ophiuchus samples.
key_parameters: Disc radius defined as aperture containing 90% of total 1.33 mm continuum flux

recipe.goal: Extract deprojected normalized 1.3 mm radial brightness profiles
recipe.method: Deproject 1.3 mm ALMA continuum brightness profiles using inclination and position angle from imfit for sources in Lupus and Ophiuchus with peak SNR > 10 x rms and where the imfit Gaussian coincides with the signal peak.
key_parameters: peak SNR > 10 x rms; imfit Gaussian coincides with signal peak; 147 radial profiles total
assumptions: At 1.3 mm the brightness profile is well correlated with the distribution of mass as a function of radius

answer_key.quantity: Visual companion multiplicity fraction in Lupus (20-4800 au)

evidence.quote: The fraction of visual multiple systems (with separations of 20–4800 au) are similar in both samples, with 12$\%$ (13/105) in Lupus and 18$\%$ (43/236) in Ophiuchus.
The frequency of visual companion multiplicity in Lupus in the range 20-4800 au is then 12% (13/105).

answer_key.quantity: Number of physically bound multiple systems identified in Lupus

evidence.quote: We identify a total of 13 multiple systems, including 11 doubles and 2 triples.
In total we report the detection of 11 potentially bound binary systems and 2 triple systems

answer_key.quantity: Number of single objects in NIR-Lupus sample

evidence.quote: | Single objects | 92 | Single class II and class III objects in Lupus |

answer_key.quantity: Combined Lupus + Ophiuchus visual multiplicity fraction (20-4000 au, flux ratio > 0.01)

evidence.quote: Considering the Lupus and Ophiuchus regions, the fraction of stellar multiplicity for circumstellar discs with visual companions (separations $\sim$20–4000 au, flux ratios $>$ 0.01) is 16%.

answer_key.quantity: Dust mass threshold below which single and multiple disc distributions are similar

evidence.quote: the distribution of disc masses and sizes are similar for single and multiple systems for M$_{\rm dust} < 50$ M$_{\oplus}$ and radii $R_{\rm dust}<$ 70 au.
The distribution of the dust mass of discs around single stars and multiple systems are similar up to M$_{\rm dust}$ = 50 M$_{\oplus}$.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum dust mass of discs around single stars in Lupus and Ophiuchus

evidence.quote: Note that the most massive discs of both Lupus and Ophiuchus have M$_{\rm dust}$ $\simeq$ 200 M$_{\oplus}$.
Higher mass discs (up to $\sim$200 M$_{\oplus}$) are only found around single stars.

answer_key.quantity: Disc dust radius threshold above which discs are only seen around single stars

evidence.quote: we find that the most massive (M$_{\rm dust}$ $>$ 50 M$_{\oplus}$) and largest ($R_{\rm dust}>$ 70 au) discs are only seen around stars lacking visual companions

answer_key.quantity: Maximum disc semi-major axis for multiple systems in combined Lupus+Ophiuchus sample

evidence.quote: From the complete samples of all the discs of Lupus and Ophiuchus we can constrain the maximum size for multiple-system discs to be $\sim$80 au, while discs around single stars can be more than 3 times larger.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum disc semi-major axis for single stars in combined sample

evidence.quote: Discs around single stars can have semi-major axes up to 300 au, while discs around multiple systems are 3 times smaller.

answer_key.quantity: KS test p-value comparing single vs multiple disc dust mass distributions in Lupus

evidence.quote: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test comparing the distributions of singles versus multiples gives a p-value of 40% for Lupus and 51% for Lupus and Ophiuchus combined.

answer_key.quantity: KS test p-value comparing single vs multiple disc dust mass distributions in Lupus + Ophiuchus

evidence.quote: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test comparing the distributions of singles versus multiples gives a p-value of 40% for Lupus and 51% for Lupus and Ophiuchus combined.

answer_key.quantity: Estimated mass of companion candidate 2MASS J16095628-3859518C

evidence.quote: From the AMES-COND evolutionary models, following the same procedure used in (cite: Zurlo2020), the object would have an estimated mass of 12 M$_{\mathrm{Jup}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Incidence of tight visual binaries (10-40 au) in Lupus and Ophiuchus

evidence.quote: The fraction of binary systems in Lupus and Ophiuchus is only 4% from the NIR-Lupus and NIR-ODISEA surveys
The incidence of tight visual binaries (with separations of 10-40 au) that are likely to prevent the formation of planets is rather low (4 %)

score_reason: ALMA disc masses and sizes are directly taken from published tables in Ansdell et al. (2018) and Lovell et al. (2020), and all ESO/ALMA program IDs and detected binaries are tabulated, though the full 105-object master table and radial profile extraction parameters are not explicitly provided.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA and VLT/NACO datasets are public, the published catalog tables in Ansdell et al. (2018) and Lovell et al. (2020) provide the exact disc masses and sizes, and the statistical comparison (Kaplan-Meier curves and KS tests) produces clear numeric benchmarks.
